spots.name: Lal Bagh
spots.summary: Lalbagh Botanical Garden or simply Lalbagh, is a botanical garden in Bengaluru, India. It was originally built by Hyder Ali in 1760, during the Sultanate of Mysore. The garden was later managed under numerous British superintendents before Indian Independence.

spots.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
spots.summary: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace, in Bangalore, India, is an example of Indo-Islamic architecture and was the summer residence of the Mysorean ruler Tipu Sultan. Hyder Ali commenced its construction within the walls of the Bangalore Fort in 1781, and it was completed during the reign of Tipu Sultan 10 years later in 1791.

spots.name: Cubbon Park
spots.summary: Sri Chamarajendra Park, formerly known as Cubbon Park is a landmark park in Bengaluru, located in the heart of the city in the Central Business District. Originally created in 1870 under Major General Richard Sankey, then British Chief Engineer of Mysore State, it covered an area of 100 acres (0.40 km2).

spots.name: Bengaluru Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bengaluru Palace is a 19th-century royal palace located in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. It was commissioned by the Maharaja of Mysore, and was completed in 1874.

spots.name: MG Road
spots.summary: Mahatma Gandhi Road also known as MG Road is a road in Bengaluru, India. It runs east from Trinity Circle at one end to Anil Kumble Circle at the other. Known as South Parade in pre-independence era, it was renamed as Mahatma Gandhi Road on 26 February 1948.

spots.name: Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum
spots.summary: The Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum (VITM), Bangalore, India, a constituent unit of the National Council of Science Museums (NCSM), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, was established in memory of Sir M. Visvesvaraya.

spots.name: Bangalore Fort
spots.summary: Bangalore Fort began construction in 1537 as a mud fort. The builder was Kempe Gowda I, a vassal of the Vijayanagara Empire and the founder of Bangalore. The then Sultan of Mysore Hyder Ali in 1761 replaced the mud fort with a stone fort and it was further improved by his son, Tipu Sultan in the late 18th century.

spots.name: Shivoham Shiva Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shivoham Shiva Temple is a Hindu temple, situated on Old Airport Road, Bangalore, India, dedicated to the Hindu deity Shiva. Built in 1995, it features a 65 feet (20 m) statue of Shiva.

spots.name: Kadu Malleshwara Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kadu Malleshwara Temple is a 17th-century A.D. Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in the Malleshwaram locality of Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. The word 'Kadu' means forest, referring here to the thick greenery all around the temple.

spots.name: Dakshinamukha Nandi Tirtha Kalyani Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sri Dakshinamukha Nandi Tirtha Kalyani Kshetra is a small temple located in front of the Gangamma temple and diagonally opposite to the Kadu Malleshwara temple on 2nd Temple Street, Malleswaram layout in the north-western area of Bangalore city, Karnataka, India.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Sri Dakshinamukha Nandi Tirtha Kalyani Kshetra

spots.name: Bengaluru Aquarium
spots.summary: Namma Bengaluru Aquarium is the second largest aquarium in India. It is located at the entrance of Cubbon Park in Bengaluru, India, and was established in 1983. It has a variety of exotic cultivable as well as marine fishes on display. It is very near to vishweshwarayya museum.

spots.name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Bengaluru

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) is an art gallery in Bangalore. It was inaugurated in the year 2009. It showcases modern Indian art and houses paintings by Raja Ravi Verma, Jamini Roy, Amrita Sher-Gil, Rabindranath Tagore and a large number of modern and contemporary artists.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Gallery of Modern Art, Bengaluru

spots.name: Government Museum, Bengaluru

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Government Museum, Bengaluru, established in 1865 by the Mysore State with the guidance of Surgeon Edward Balfour who founded the museum in Madras and supported by the Chief Commissioner of Mysore, L.B. Bowring, is one of the oldest museums in India and the second oldest museum in South India.

spots.name: Church Street, Bengaluru
spots.summary: Church Street is a busy street in the Central Business District of Bengaluru, India. It is a 750-metre stretch from Brigade Road to St. Mark's Road, running parallel to M G Road. The street is named for St. Mark's Cathedral to which it leads.

spots.name: Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ragigudda Sree Prasanna Anjaneyaswamy Temple, commonly referred to as Ragigudda Temple or Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple is a temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman, spread across 5 acres also having a hillock in Jayanagara 9th Block area n Bengaluru, Karnataka, India.

spots.name: Dodda Basavana Gudi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dodda Basavana Gudi is situated in Bull Temple Road, Basavanagudi, area of South Bengaluru, part of the largest city of the Indian state of Karnataka. The Hindu temple is inside a park called Bugle Rock.

spots.name: Venkatappa Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Venkatappa Art Gallery (VAG) is situated in Bangalore, India, in the vicinity of Cubbon Park and next to the Bangalore Museum as well as the Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum. This art gallery showcases the artworks of artist K. Venkatappa. It attracts artists and art lovers from all over Karnataka.

spots.name: Museum of Art & Photography

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Museum of Art and Photography (MAP) is a private Indian art museum based in Bangalore with a collection of Indian art, textiles, photography, craft, and design objects spanning from the twelfth century to the present.

spots.name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
spots.summary: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple, or Sri Gangaadhareshwara, also Gavipuram Cave Temple, an example of Indian rock-cut architecture, is located in Bengaluru in the state of Karnataka in India.

spots.name: Statue of Queen Victoria
spots.summary: The Statue of Queen Victoria, Bangalore, is located at Queen's Park, next to Cubbon Park, Bangalore Cantonment, at the junction of 3 roads, at the border between the Cantonment and the Bangalore Pete. The statue was unveiled on 5 February 1906 by the then Prince of Wales, George Frederick Ernest Albert.

spots.name: Domlur Chokkanathaswamy temple
spots.summary: Chokkanathaswamy temple, at Domlur in the Indian city of Bangalore, Karnataka, India, is dedicated to the deity known as Chokkanathaswamy or Chokka Perumal. It is one of the oldest temples in the city.

spots.name: National Military Memorial
spots.summary: National Military Memorial is a memorial park located in Bengaluru and established by the Government of Karnataka in 2013 to honour the men and families of martyrs who died in the service of the nation.

spots.name: Kote Venkataramana Temple, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kote Venkataramana Temple is a Hindu temple in Krishnarajendra Road, Bangalore, India dedicated to the Hindu god Venkateshwara. The temple was built in 1689 in Dravidian and Vijayanagara style by King Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar, then ruler of Mysore.

spots.name: Rangoli Gardens

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Rangoli Gardens is a model arts heritage village, located in Jakkur, Bangalore. Rangoli Gardens documents how rural people of Karnataka lived, 100 to 200 years ago. This village exhibits more than 1,000 life-size sculptures.

spots.name: Ranga Shankara
spots.summary: Ranga Shankara is one of Bangalore's well known theatres. It is located in the south Bangalore area of J.P Nagar and is run by the Sanket Trust. The auditorium, which opened in 2004, was envisioned by Arundathi Nag, in remembrance of her late husband, Shankar Nag, who was a renowned actor in the Kannada film industry.

spots.name: Freedom Park, Bengaluru
spots.summary: Freedom Park is located in the Central Business District of the city of Bengaluru, Karnataka, India. It was formerly the Central Jail.

spots.name: St. Mark's Cathedral, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mark's Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Mark the Evangelist, is the cathedral of the Diocese of Central Karnataka of the Church of South India.

spots.name: Cunningham Road
spots.summary: Cunningham Road is one of the busiest commercial streets of Bangalore, the state capital of Karnataka, India. It is located in the Vasanthnagar area of the city. The road is named after Francis Cunningham, who was an officer in the Madras Army and a member of the Mysore Commission.

spots.name: Sri Pralayakala Veerabadrar temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sri Pralayakala Veerabhadra temple, located in Gavipura, Guddadahallii, Bangalore, is a temple dedicated to the Hindu deity Pralayakala Veerabadra.

spots.name: Old Madiwala Someshwara Temple, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Old Madiwala Sri Someshwara Temple located in Bangalore city, Karnataka, India is dedicated to the deity Someshwara. It is one among the oldest temples in the city and dates back to the Chola Empire period. The temple belongs to the early 12th century.(1247 AD).

spots.name: Kempegowda Museum
spots.summary: Kempegowda Museum is a government museum located in the city of Bangalore, in the state of Karnataka, India. It was established in the year 2011 is dedicated to Yelahanka chieftain Kempegowda (1513-1569) who was the founder of Bangalore city. The museum is located on the first floor of Mayo Hall.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Church, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Trinity Church, located at Trinity circle at the east end of the MG Road, is an Anglican church and a major landmark in Bengaluru. It was built in 1851, for the British Regiment stationed there.

spots.name: Malleshwaram inscriptions and hero stones

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Malleshwara is a northwestern locality in Bengaluru, recognized as one of the city's oldest planned areas.

spots.name: Plaza Theatre
spots.summary: Plaza was a film theatre located in the city of Bangalore, India. It used to be on M. G. Road in the Bangalore Cantonment area. It was built in 1936 and mostly screened Hollywood movies.

spots.name: Agara inscriptions and hero stones

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Agara inscriptions and hero stones are three passages of Kannada text inscribed on memorial stones found in or around Agara, a Panchayat-village located on the Outer Ring Road near Koramangala and HSR Layout in Bengaluru, India.

spots.name: Sree Kanteerava Stadium
spots.summary: Sree Kanteerava Outdoor Stadium, also known as Sampangi Outdoor Stadium, is a multi-purpose stadium in Bengaluru, India. It houses a running track, a volleyball court, and two outdoor rock climbing walls. The stadium is owned by the Department of Youth Empowerment and Sports, Government of Karnataka.

spots.name: Hudson Memorial Church, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hudson Memorial Church is located in the Bangalore Pete, Hudson Circle, surrounded by the Office of the Bangalore Corporation, Ulsoor Gate Police Station, Cubbon Park and Kanteerava Stadium. The church was established in 1904, and is a Kannada CSI church of the Bangalore Diocese.

spots.name: Hebbal-Kittayya inscription

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hebbal is a locality situated in the northern part of Bengaluru, is recognized as one of Bengaluru’s oldest regions, with documented history extending back at least 1,300 years. Originally marking the northern boundary of the city, Bengaluru has since expanded significantly northward.

spots.name: St. Paul's Church, Bengaluru

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Paul's Church is located in the corner of Old Poor House Road, and Bowring Hospital Road, next to the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore Cantonment, India. St. Paul's has the distinction of being the very first Tamil Anglican Church in the erstwhile Mysore State. St.

spots.name: Bangalore Football Stadium
spots.summary: The Bangalore Football Stadium is a football stadium in Bengaluru, Karnataka. It has served as a venue in three editions of the I-League, then top-tier football league in the country. The stadium was the home of Bengaluru FC for one season, when they won the I-League trophy in their first attempt.

spots.name: Agara inscription
spots.summary: The Agara inscriptions and hero stones are three passages of Kannada text inscribed on memorial stones found in or around Agara, a Panchayat-village located on the Outer Ring Road near Koramangala and HSR Layout in Bengaluru, India.

spots.name: Gallery G
spots.summary: Gallery G is an Indian art gallery and resource based in Bangalore. It provides informed access to art and consultancy services for investors, architects, interior designers and organizes traveling art shows.

spots.name: Science Gallery Bengaluru

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Inaugurated in 2024, this museum holds various artistic exhibitions and lectures with a view to science outreach and art-science collaborations. It does not have any permanent collection, but rather a series of temporary exhibitions each year.

spots.name: Attara Kacheri
spots.summary: A two-storey neoclassical red-painted stone and brick building, hosting the High Court of Karnataka. It was a secretariat of eighteen departments, built under the reign of king Devaraja Wadiyar II in 1701. The main structure of the building is surrounded on all sides by porticoes and verandahs.
